tools.name: oculon_radar
tools.description: Global anomaly radar. Finds what the world is suddenly paying attention to right now (Wikipedia readership spikes, Hacker News traction, Polymarket swings, strong earthquakes, severe natural events) and fuses items about the same subject into corroborated signals with evidence.

tools.name: oculon_footprint
tools.description: Pre-release footprints of a domain: hostnames that newly appeared in Certificate Transparency logs, pages newly archived by the Wayback Machine, and newly created public GitHub repos. Good for spotting unannounced products.

tools.name: oculon_hype
tools.description: Hype-cycle phase of a topic (DORMANT, EMERGING, RISING, PEAK, COOLING, STEADY) from 8 weeks of Wikipedia readers, Hacker News stories, global news share (GDELT), arXiv papers and new GitHub repos.

tools.name: oculon_aircraft
tools.description: Track one aircraft by registration (e.g. N628TS) or ICAO hex: type, registered owner, live position from ADS-B, nearest airport, and movement since the previous check.

tools.name: oculon_military_air
tools.description: Worldwide military air traffic from open ADS-B data, grouped by region, with notable roles (tanker, AWACS, ISR, bomber, maritime patrol) and surges versus the region history.

tools.name: oculon_dossier
tools.description: Dossier on a company, person or project: Wikipedia profile and readership spike, Hacker News stories, news, related Polymarket markets, new GitHub repos, SEC filings (if enabled), merged into one timeline with a fused signal.

tools.name: oculon_natural_events
tools.description: Open natural events from NASA EONET (tropical cyclones, wildfires, volcanoes, floods, icebergs) with a severity score.

tools.name: oculon_night_lights
tools.description: Night-time lights of a place from NASA VIIRS satellite data: recent nights versus a baseline month. A sharp drop can indicate blackout, conflict or evacuation; a rise can indicate new activity.

tools.name: oculon_satellite_image
tools.description: True-color satellite image (NASA MODIS, about 250 m) of a place for a date. Returns the image.

tools.name: oculon_sentinel_image
tools.description: Sharp satellite image (Copernicus Sentinel-2, 10 m per pixel; or Sentinel-1 radar that sees through clouds) of a place, least cloudy pass in the window ending on the date. Returns the image.

tools.name: oculon_scoreboard
tools.description: Forecast track record: counts, Brier scores of the model and of the market, and skill versus the market.

tools.name: oculon_verify_proof
tools.description: Verify a forecast proof: recompute its hash, check the Merkle path, and check the Bitcoin attestation against the block merkle root. Returns VERIFIED, PENDING, NOT_STAMPED, TAMPERED or ERROR.

tools.name: oculon_wallet
tools.description: On-chain wallet intelligence for an EVM (0x...) or Solana address: portfolio value and top holdings, first transaction and age, recent transactions, risk labels (GoPlus, Webacy), and balance on Robinhood Chain.

tools.name: oculon_token
tools.description: Token contract check: honeypot and owner-power flags, buy/sell tax and holders (GoPlus), DEX pairs and liquidity (DexScreener), price and market cap (CoinGecko). Returns DANGER, CAUTION, OK or UNKNOWN with reasons.

tools.name: oculon_ships
tools.description: Live vessels around a port or sea area from AIS (aisstream.io), listening for a number of seconds: totals, moving vs anchored/moored, vessel types (cargo, tanker, military...), names. Coverage depends on community receivers; an empty result says so.

tools.name: oculon_ship
tools.description: Follow one ship by its 9-digit MMSI and return its latest AIS position, speed and status if it reports within the window.

tools.name: oculon_robinhood
tools.description: Robinhood Chain (id 4663) right now: chain activity, trending pools and pools created in the last hours, each with risk flags (thin liquidity, buys without sells, sudden dumps).

tools.name: oculon_robinhood_token
tools.description: Risk read on a Robinhood Chain token: contract verification, top-10 holder concentration, holders, and pool behavior. Returns DANGER, CAUTION, OK or UNKNOWN with reasons.

tools.name: oculon_robinhood_deployer
tools.description: Robinhood Chain deployer reputation: from a token or deployer address, find every token that wallet launched (directly or through a launchpad) and how many are dead now. Flags serial launchers.

tools.name: oculon_space_weather
tools.description: Current space weather from NOAA SWPC: planetary K index, geomagnetic storm level (G1-G5) and the strongest solar flare of the last 7 days.

tools.name: oculon_air_quality
tools.description: Latest PM2.5 air quality from monitoring stations near a place (OpenAQ), with the US EPA category.

tools.name: oculon_url_check
tools.description: Is a link dangerous? Checks Google Safe Browsing, URLhaus (abuse.ch), urlscan.io scan history, domain age and registrar (RDAP), and warning signs in the URL itself (brand names on other domains, punycode, risky TLDs). Returns a verdict (malicious, suspicious, no known threats), a 0-100 risk and the

tools.name: oculon_audit
tools.description: Dependency audit for developers. Pass the text of a package.json or requirements.txt, or items like "npm:express@4.17.1 pypi:requests==2.19.0". For each package: known vulnerabilities with CVSS, deprecation, last release, versions behind, OpenSSF Scorecard and maintenance, license; plus a 0-100 risk

tools.name: oculon_fact_check
tools.description: Fact check a claim, or the main claim of a news link. Finds published fact checks (Google Fact Check Tools: Snopes, AFP, PolitiFact, Full Fact and others) and current reporting, then gives a verdict (true, mostly true, mixed, misleading, false, unverified) with a confidence and a summary that cites

tools.name: oculon_travel
tools.description: Travel and place risk brief for the coming week: US State Department and UK FCDO advice, 7-day weather warnings (storms, heavy rain, gusts, heat, cold, UV), PM2.5 air quality, WHO disease outbreak news, GDACS disaster alerts, nearby earthquakes, satellite heat detections and confirmed internet outag

tools.name: oculon_scam_check
tools.description: Is this message a scam? Paste an SMS, email or chat message. Every link is checked (Safe Browsing, URLhaus, urlscan.io, domain age, look-alikes), the sender domain is compared with any brand it mentions, and known scam patterns are matched (parcel fees, account locked, one-time codes, gift cards or

tools.name: oculon_recall
tools.description: Is this car or product recalled? Pass a 17-character VIN, "year make model" (e.g. "2018 Honda Accord"), or a product name ("stroller", "peanut butter"). Vehicles: NHTSA safety recalls with do-not-drive and park-outside warnings. Products: CPSC consumer recalls and FDA food, drug and device enforceme

tools.name: oculon_email_security
tools.description: Can someone send email that looks like it comes from this domain? Checks SPF, DMARC, DKIM, MTA-STS, TLS reporting, BIMI, CAA and DNSSEC from public DNS, and returns a verdict (spoofable, partly protected, protected), a 0-100 score and the fixes in order.

tools.name: oculon_ip_check
tools.description: Who runs this IP address, and is it known for abuse? Pass an IPv4 or IPv6 address, or a domain (its first address is checked). Returns network (ASN, owner, type), location, flags (Tor exit, proxy, hosting, internet scanner, known benign service), AbuseIPDB reports, GreyNoise scanner status, AlienVau

tools.name: oculon_hash_check
tools.description: Is this file known malware, a known good file, or unknown? Pass an MD5, SHA-1 or SHA-256 hash. Checks CIRCL hashlookup (NIST NSRL and other known-software sets), MalwareBazaar, ThreatFox, AlienVault OTX and VirusTotal, and returns a verdict, the malware family when known, the reasons and what to do.

tools.name: oculon_ransomware
tools.description: Ransomware leak-site claims collected by ransomware.live. Leave query empty for the newest claims, or pass a two-letter country code ("DE"), a sector ("Healthcare", "Manufacturing") or a company name or domain. Returns victims with group, country, sector and dates, plus counts by group, country and

tools.name: oculon_company_lookup
tools.description: Is this company or supplier real? Pass an EU VAT number (checked live in the European Commission VIES service: valid or not, registered name and address), a 20-character LEI, or a company name (Global LEI Index: legal name, registered address, status, registration number, ultimate parent). Useful be

tools.name: oculon_breaches
tools.description: Data breaches from Have I Been Pwned: leave domain empty for the newest breaches, or pass a domain or company name for all of its breaches, with date, accounts affected and the kinds of data exposed.

tools.name: oculon_phone_check
tools.description: Who is behind this phone number? Pass it in international format (+44 20 7946 0958), or a national number with country. Returns country, line type (mobile, landline, VoIP, premium rate), carrier and location when known, and warnings for premium-rate numbers, UK 070 personal numbers and the Caribbean

tools.name: oculon_prove_status
tools.description: Look up a Bitcoin timestamp made with oculon_prove or on oculon.live/prove by the file's SHA-256: pending, or confirmed in Bitcoin block N at time T. To verify a file was timestamped, hash it and look the hash up.

tools.name: oculon_is_it_down
tools.description: Is a popular service down right now? Reads official status pages (GitHub, Discord, Reddit, OpenAI, Claude, Cloudflare, Zoom, Slack, Coinbase and ~25 more): overall state, components with problems and open incidents. For X, Google, YouTube, Instagram, Facebook, WhatsApp, Telegram, TikTok, Spotify, Ne

tools.name: oculon_charity_check
tools.description: Check a US-registered nonprofit before donating, by name or EIN (ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer, IRS data): matches with city, state, NTEE category and 501(c) subsection; for the chosen organisation the ruling year, deductibility and latest Form 990 filings with revenue, expenses and assets. Warns on

tools.name: oculon_brand_shield
tools.description: Which domains are imitating this brand right now? Combines lookalike domains that exist in DNS, certificates from the last 90 days whose names contain the brand (Certificate Transparency via crt.sh) and are not the brand's own, DNS resolution, and the URL check on the most suspicious live ones. Each

tools.name: oculon_wire
tools.description: Oculon Wire: the strongest signals Oculon stored in the last 24 hours, at most six, one per desk first (internet, air and sea, hazards, cyber, markets, space). Each line is a stored signal with its source names and time; nothing is generated. Pass a UTC date (YYYY-MM-DD) for a past day.

tools.name: oculon_scam_trends
tools.description: Scam Trends: what people checked with this Oculon server in the last 7 days, as counts only: checks by kind, verdict split, most common scam patterns and link warning signs, most impersonated brands, top-level domains of flagged links, with the week before for change. No checked input is ever return

tools.name: oculon_rescue
tools.description: What to do after a scam: a merged checklist for the next 10 minutes, today and this week, for one or more situations (link, password, code, seed, signed, card, bank, crypto, remote, id, takeover), plus official reporting links for a country (US, GB, CA, AU, NZ, IE, FR, NL, ES, SG, EU, OTHER). Fixed

tools.name: oculon_checkup
tools.description: Score a personal security checkup 0-100 with a grade A-F and the top fixes. Give results already measured (password found in breach lists yes/no and count, email domain spoofing verdict, number of breaches for the email domain, risky wallet approvals) and habit answers: passwordManager yes|no, twoFa

tools.name: oculon_spot_the_scam
tools.description: Today's Spot the Scam round: 8 defanged links, the same for everyone on a UTC date, mixing real recently blocklisted phishing domains (ScamSniffer) with real official sign-in pages, each with the answer and a code-derived explanation. If the feed is down no round is built.

tools.name: oculon_iban_check
tools.description: Check an IBAN before paying an invoice, fully offline: country, length, ISO 13616 mod-97 check digits and the bank code. Pass the supplier country to flag an account held in another country, a common sign of invoice fraud. A valid IBAN does not prove who owns the account.

tools.name: oculon_email_headers
tools.description: Analyze the raw headers of a suspicious email: SPF, DKIM and DMARC results recorded by the receiving server, the Received path, the origin IP and its country, and spoofing signs (From differs from the envelope sender, Reply-To elsewhere, a display name posing as an address). Returns a verdict and ri

tools.name: oculon_lookalike_domains
tools.description: Find lookalike domains of a brand that a phisher could use: typos, swapped letters, homoglyphs, extra words and other endings that exist in DNS (with mail servers), plus certificates issued in the last 90 days for any name containing the brand (Certificate Transparency).

tools.name: oculon_honeypot_check
tools.description: Can this token be sold? Simulates a buy and a sell on the token's main pool and replays recent holders' sells (honeypot.is): honeypot verdict, buy and sell tax, holders who could not sell, unpublished or upgradeable contracts. Chains: eth, bsc, base.

tools.name: oculon_address_check
tools.description: Check a crypto address before sending funds, without API keys: chain from the address format (Bitcoin, EVM, Solana, Tron), US OFAC sanctions, and balance, transaction count and labels from free explorers (mempool.space, Blockscout, Solana RPC). Flags unused addresses and contracts posing as wallets.

tools.name: oculon_doc_check
tools.description: Was this invoice, bank statement or payment screenshot edited? Reads a PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, JPEG or PNG: macros, remote templates, DDE fields, embedded objects and hidden sheets in Office files, the programs that made and saved it (online PDF editors, image editors), creation vs modificatio

tools.name: oculon_approvals
tools.description: Who can take tokens out of this wallet right now: every ERC-20 and NFT approval the wallet signed (Etherscan logs), re-read on chain so revoked ones drop out. Spenders are named (Uniswap, 1inch, OpenSea...) or flagged: plain wallets, unverified contracts and unknown contracts with unlimited access.

tools.name: oculon_contract_risk
tools.description: What the owner of a token contract can still do to holders: mint, blacklist, pause trading, change taxes, limit wallets, change balances, upgrade the code (proxy), self-destruct. Read from verified source (Sourcify, Etherscan) or, for unverified contracts, from selectors in the bytecode. Plus curren

tools.name: oculon_signature_check
tools.description: Decode what a wallet signature request really allows before signing: EIP-712 typed data (ERC-2612 and DAI permits, Uniswap Permit2 allowances and transfers, Seaport orders that give NFTs away for nothing), transaction calldata or a {to, data, value} object (approve, setApprovalForAll, transfers, Per

tools.name: oculon_address_poisoning
tools.description: Has someone planted lookalike addresses in this wallet's history? Finds addresses that share the first and last characters with ones the wallet really paid, zero-value transfers it never signed, and fake USDT/USDC tokens, and says whether funds were already sent to a lookalike. Chains: eth, arbitrum

tools.name: oculon_trace_funds
tools.description: Follow where money went from an address (for example a scammer or a drained wallet): the largest outgoing flows priced in USD, hop by hop, until an exchange (where funds can be frozen), a mixer, a bridge, a contract or a sanctioned address. Labels from the open eth-labels dataset, transaction hashes

tools.name: oculon_screenshot_check
tools.description: Is the message in this screenshot a scam? A free vision model (Gemini) transcribes the visible text verbatim and lists links, handles, phone numbers, amounts and brands, and names the screen kind (chat, email, SMS, web page, ad, social post). The verdict comes from the scam check run in code on that

tools.name: oculon_terms_read
tools.description: Read terms of service, a privacy policy or a subscription, rental or employment contract and flag the clauses worth reading twice: automatic renewal, cancellation fees and no refunds, forced arbitration and class action or jury waivers, selling or sharing personal data, location, biometric and conta

tools.name: oculon_image_check
tools.description: Was this image made by AI, edited, or taken with a camera? Reads C2PA Content Credentials (generator app, actions, AI source type, organizations in the signing certificates), IPTC digital source type, generator settings and prompts left by Stable Diffusion, ComfyUI, NovelAI, InvokeAI and Midjourney,

tools.name: oculon_qr_check
tools.description: Read the QR code in a photo or screenshot (PNG or baseline JPEG, versions 1-15) and check where it leads: links go through the URL check (Safe Browsing, URLhaus, domain age, lookalikes, shorteners), crypto payment codes and addresses through the address check, SEPA payment codes get their IBAN check

tools.name: oculon_repo_check
tools.description: Is this GitHub repository safe to clone and run? Built for fake job tests and "run our bot" scams: install hooks (npm preinstall/postinstall, setup.py, VS Code tasks that run on folder open), code that downloads and runs code, wallet extension and browser password theft, Discord/Telegram webhooks, o

tools.name: oculon_domain_report
tools.description: One report for a domain, all parts run together: link check of the site, email protection (SPF, DKIM, DMARC), what it exposes to the internet (open ports, CVEs), lookalike domains, and the company behind the name. Each part keeps its verdict and sources; PDF report available through the check id.

tools.name: oculon_wallet_report
tools.description: One report for a wallet or token address. Wallet: address check (sanctions, activity), active approvals, address poisoning and where funds went. Token contract: contract risk, sell simulation and address check. PDF report available through the check id.

tools.name: oculon_site_check
tools.description: Open a web page and look for wallet drainers and phishing: wallet connection code next to permit, Permit2, setApprovalForAll or unlimited approve requests, a receiver address written into the script, token-balance APIs used to rank what to take, known drainer kits, seed phrase and login forms on the

tools.name: oculon_tx_explain
tools.description: Explain a transaction in plain words: who called what, every token and NFT transfer, approvals given or removed, and the fee. Flags tokens taken from a wallet in a transaction it did not send (an earlier approval or permit being used), approvals to plain wallets or unverified contracts, and NFT coll

tools.name: oculon_token_creator
tools.description: Who created this token and what is their record: the creator wallet and date, the other contracts it deployed, which of those tokens are dead today (no pool or under $1,000 of liquidity), its wallet age, and who first funded it (exchange or mixer, from eth-labels). Chains: eth, arbitrum, polygon.

tools.name: oculon_email_file
tools.description: Check a whole email file (.eml): SPF, DKIM, DMARC and spoofing in the headers, the message and every link through the scam check, and each attachment through the document check (PDF, Office), the QR reader and image check (images), or the malware hash lookup. Flags risky attachment types (programs,

tools.name: oculon_apk_check
tools.description: Is this Android app (APK) safe to install? Reads its manifest: package, version, every permission, and the ones banking trojans use (reading SMS codes, accessibility services, drawing over other apps, notification access, device admin, installing other apps); the signing certificate (debug keys flag

tools.name: oculon_job_check
tools.description: Is this job offer a scam? Matches the patterns of job scams in the message (fees before you start, paid tasks you top up, crypto pay, pay that does not fit the work, contact only through WhatsApp or Telegram, no interview, early requests for ID or bank details, check-cashing, coding test tasks that

tools.name: oculon_photo_location
tools.description: Where and when was this photo taken? GPS position and capture time from its EXIF data, the place name (OpenStreetMap), and the weather and daylight at that place and hour (Open-Meteo, sun position), so claims about a photo can be checked. Flags capture and GPS times that disagree. EXIF can be edited

tools.name: oculon_archive
tools.description: Save a web page as evidence: asks the Wayback Machine to save it now and records the page status, final address, title and SHA-256 of what was served. Falls back to the newest existing snapshot when saving fails.

tools.name: oculon_invite_check
tools.description: What is behind a Telegram (t.me) or Discord (discord.gg) invite before joining: name, members and online, verified badge, Telegram scam or fake labels, server creation date, and the fake support or fake project pattern (brand plus "official", "support", "airdrop" without a verified badge).

tools.name: oculon_stock_token
tools.description: Robinhood Stock Tokens (tokenized shares on Robinhood Chain), from Robinhood's official API. A ticker (TSLA) gives the official contract, ISIN, which sessions trade, the live bid and ask per token (adjusted by the corporate-action multiplier), daily range, volume, supply on chain, and upcoming divid

tools.name: oculon_replay
tools.description: Replay log of an earlier check by its check id: the verdict, what changed since the check before it, and every source called in order with status and time.

tools.name: oculon_status
tools.description: Which Oculon sources are up, slow, degraded or down, from real calls in the last hours: success rate, median time, last error, and sources being skipped (a mirror or cached data answers instead).

tools.name: oculon_satellites
tools.description: Satellites from CelesTrak. Leave query empty for everything launched in the last 30 days, grouped by launch. Or pass a satellite name ("ISS", "starlink-1007") or NORAD catalog number for its orbit (perigee, apogee, period, inclination, regime), owner, launch date and status.

tools.name: oculon_papers
tools.description: Research brief on a topic: the most cited papers of recent years, the newest relevant ones, papers per year (is the field growing?), PubMed counts for medical topics, and a short overview that cites the numbered papers. Sources: OpenAlex, PubMed, Semantic Scholar.

tools.name: oculon_country
tools.description: Country brief: GDP, growth, GDP per person, inflation, unemployment and population (World Bank), IMF growth and inflation outlook, head of state and government, capital, currency and its rate to the US dollar, US and UK travel advice, internet outages, disaster alerts and the latest headlines.

tools.name: oculon_airport
tools.description: Is an airport running normally? Current METAR and TAF (flight category, wind, visibility, ceiling), FAA ground stops, delay programs and closures for US airports, and aircraft squawking an emergency within 150 km. Accepts IATA (JFK), ICAO (EGLL) or a name.

tools.name: oculon_monitor
tools.description: Create a monitor from a plain-language request, e.g. "tell me when there is an internet outage in Iran", "watch critical CVEs for nginx", "earthquakes above 6 near Tokyo", "news about OpenAI", "travel risk changes for Bangkok". It becomes a watch rule that is re-checked on a schedule and reports onl

tools.name: oculon_web_search
tools.description: Search the web (Tavily, Exa fallback). Returns titles, URLs, snippets and dates.

tools.name: oculon_read_page
tools.description: Fetch a web page and return its readable text (Jina Reader, Firecrawl fallback), capped at about 6000 characters.

tools.name: oculon_ask
tools.description: Ask Oculon a question in plain language. An agent picks and calls Oculon tools (radar, dossiers, aircraft, satellites, on-chain, web) and answers with sources.

tools.name: oculon_case_list
tools.description: List case files with their confidence, number of findings and whether they are watched.

tools.name: oculon_case_show
tools.description: Show one case file in full.

tools.name: oculon_narratives
tools.description: News narratives tracked across days (storylines such as a company crisis or an IPO), with stories per day and phase. Set run=true to first group the latest headlines.

tools.name: oculon_health
tools.description: Company early-warning score 0-100 from hiring momentum, new federal lawsuits, insider selling, news tone, GitHub shipping and the stock move, with every component explained and a 30-day history.

tools.name: oculon_impact
tools.description: People exposed to current M6+ earthquakes and severe storms (Wikidata settlement populations within the affected radius, plus night-light change when enough nights have passed). Give a place to estimate exposure around it instead.

tools.name: oculon_contradictions
tools.description: Read several independent articles on a topic and list factual claims that conflict between them (numbers, dates, names, denials), each side with its source URL.

tools.name: oculon_sanctions
tools.description: Screen against the US OFAC sanctions (SDN) list: a wallet address (also checks whether it transacted directly with a listed address), a vessel IMO number, or the exact name of a company, person or vessel. Returns SANCTIONED, EXPOSED or CLEAR.

tools.name: oculon_markets_crosscheck
tools.description: Cross-check Polymarket against Kalshi and Manifold: an LLM confirms which markets ask exactly the same question, then gaps between venues are listed. A big gap means one crowd is wrong or knows something first.

tools.name: oculon_launches
tools.description: Launch radar for a company: new Hugging Face models/datasets/Spaces, new iOS apps and app updates, new npm packages under its scope, and (with a domain) new hostnames, pages and repos.

tools.name: oculon_rewind
tools.description: Time machine: what Oculon would have seen on a past date. Wikipedia spikes measured against the weeks before, top Hacker News stories, strong earthquakes and that day's Guardian headlines, fused across sources.

tools.name: oculon_fence_list
tools.description: List geofences with their boxes and what each watches.

tools.name: oculon_fence_check
tools.description: Check every geofence now and report what is new inside each since the previous check.

tools.name: oculon_watch_list
tools.description: List the watchlist: targets Oculon re-checks for changes (companies, domains, wallets, tokens, planes, topics, night lights, air quality).

tools.name: oculon_brief
tools.description: Today's brief: the strongest signals of the last 24 hours and watchlist changes, summarized.

tools.name: oculon_signals
tools.description: Most recent signals produced by any Oculon module, with scores and evidence.

tools.name: oculon_entity
tools.description: Look up an entity in the Oculon graph and its neighbors. Ids look like "domain:openai.com", "org:nvidia", "aircraft:a835af", "company:falcon landing llc".

tools.name: oculon_connect
tools.description: How two things are connected in the Oculon graph: shortest path of typed edges between them (names or ids). Duplicates such as org:nvidia and company:nvidia are merged first.

tools.name: oculon_social_pulse
tools.description: What people are posting about a subject right now on X, Reddit, TikTok (paid Apify, small daily budget) and Bluesky: post counts per platform, pace over the last day when measurable, most engaged and latest posts with links.

tools.name: oculon_podcast
tools.description: Find recent podcast episodes about a subject and transcribe the newest English one (Deepgram, paid per minute with a daily budget): machine summary, topics, and timestamped passages that mention the subject.

tools.name: oculon_listen
tools.description: Transcribe a public audio or video FILE URL (mp3, mp4, wav...; not a YouTube page) with Deepgram and return a machine summary, topics and timestamped passages that mention the subject.

tools.name: oculon_exposure
tools.description: A domain's internet exposure: resolves its main hosts and known subdomains, then lists open ports, software and known CVEs per IP from Shodan InternetDB (free). CDN edges are marked.

tools.name: oculon_dark_ships
tools.description: Vessels that deliberately switched off AIS near a place (port, strait, sea) in the last days, from Global Fishing Watch: where they went dark and reappeared, for how long. Coverage is strongest for fishing and carrier vessels.

tools.name: oculon_vessel
tools.description: Vessel identity from a name, MMSI or IMO (Global Fishing Watch registry data): flag history, type, owners, earlier names, first and last AIS transmission, OFAC sanctions check on the IMO.

tools.name: oculon_fires
tools.description: Active fires and thermal hotspots near a place in the last 1-5 days from NASA FIRMS (VIIRS satellites): clusters with detection count and fire radiative power. Catches wildfires, industrial fires and strikes on infrastructure.

tools.name: oculon_cloud_outages
tools.description: Current outages on major internet platforms: official status pages of GitHub, Cloudflare, OpenAI, Anthropic, Discord, Reddit, Vercel, npm and others, plus AWS, Azure and Google Cloud incidents.

tools.name: oculon_bgp
tools.description: BGP routing. "world": global BGP hijacks and route leaks (Cloudflare Radar) with DDoS target countries. Two-letter country code: visible IPv4/IPv6 prefixes per hour and change versus the median (shutdowns and cable cuts show as drops), plus incidents involving it. AS number: visibility, prefixes, ne

tools.name: oculon_vulns
tools.description: Vulnerabilities newly exploited in the wild (CISA KEV) with EPSS odds and due dates, new critical CVEs (NVD) and critical package advisories (GitHub), optionally for one vendor.

tools.name: oculon_cve
tools.description: One CVE in depth: CVSS, CWE, affected products, EPSS exploitation probability and 30-day trend, CISA KEV status, affected packages with fixed versions (OSV, GitHub).

tools.name: oculon_package_vulns
tools.description: Known vulnerabilities of a software package (OSV.dev), optionally for one version, flagged when exploited in the wild.

tools.name: oculon_regs
